ABSTRACT  
15 July 2020  
Keywords:  
Derivation,  
Verbs, African, Masaaba. In this article, the researcher explains how verbs in African languages are derived to convey different meanings. This is done by referring to Masaaba, a language spoken by the Masaaba people in Uganda. Verb derivation is a common phenomenon and is practiced in various languages. Therefore, in this article, the researcher describes the verb derivation process in the Masaaba language. He presents a collection of verbs and explains how speakers derive them. In addition, the researcher discusses how these verbs are used in sentences. The researcher does this because many African languages have not been studied, and there are many fascinating aspects that are unknown to the world. In this work, the researcher writes various verbs in the original language and then translates them into Swahili. The aim of this study is, firstly, to demonstrate the process of verb derivation in Masaaba; secondly, to explain the different meanings that result from verb derivation; and thirdly, to show that Masaaba is a language that continues to grow like other African languages. The research approach was field-based. Using this approach, the researcher visited the field where they conducted interviews with their respondents. The responses of the respondents constituted the data needed by the researcher. In conclusion, the findings of this research indicate that Kimasaaba, like other African languages, has a great number of verbs that are derived and facilitate the speakers’ discourse. A verb is a word that describes the state of an action. A single verb can be derived and express different states of actions. Typically, there are forms such as the active, reciprocal, passive, stative, and causative in many Bantu languages. Therefore, in this work, the researcher lists various Kimasaaba verbs, which is the language of the Bamasaaba, and translates them into Swahili. It should be noted early on that there are different dialects of Kimasaaba. Therefore, in this research, the researcher focused on a particular dialect known as ‘Lubuuya.’ After translating the verbs, the researcher explains the process of verb derivation. Having described how these verbs are derived, the researcher clarifies how they are used in sentences. The researcher does so by considering the explanations of various authors regarding verb derivation. Finally, the researcher concludes the work by providing his views on important matters related to the research. RESEARCH QUESTION  
In this study, the researcher employed the interview method. Using this approach, the researcher went out into the field to meet the respondents. Before conducting the interviews, the researcher explained to the respondents the purpose of the research. After doing so, the researcher proceeded to conduct interviews with them. The respondents consisted of 50 women and 50 men. The researcher ensured that there was an equal number of women and men due to the issue of gender equality. These respondents were selected using the purposive sampling method. Using this method, the researcher continued conversations with the respondents as he met them. He did not use any special procedure in selecting the respondents. The researcher had a set of questions that he used during the interviews. The researcher used this guide to ensure that he would not forget any important points. The discussions that were conducted largely focused on verb derivation. After mentioning a verb, the researcher asked how to derive it in different contexts. According to the researcher, there are very many ethnic groups in Africa. Each ethnic group has its own indigenous language. Therefore, there are numerous languages spoken across the continent. However, the majority of these languages have not been researched, and there is a great deal that these languages convey which is still unknown to the world. There are very few African languages that have been thoroughly studied.

In grammar, derivation is the ability of a root or stem to be affixed with a morpheme at its beginning or end. The result is to expand the meaning of the given word. This is the function of every affix—to build new roots and stems of words, which are called derivational stems or roots. We can also say that this is the function of derivational affixes or formative affixes. Often, formative affixes appear at the end of the stem or root. Accordingly, they have continued to be called suffix-formative affixes. In this context, derivation involves two types of affixes: (a) Semantic Affixes, which appear at the beginning of the root of a word. These affixes can expand the meaning of a word without changing its root. For example: tu-ta-m-pig-an-ish-a. A participial verb, which takes the same form as “ni” or “si”, is considered to link other elements in a sentence. Example: Musa is a teacher, the town of Msoma is smaller than the town of Mwanza, this young man is not honest, I am not a student. Based on the context of these sentences, it appears that these elements are considered to link the constituents on the left and right sides of the verb itself. These sentences are in the present tense. If these sentences are changed to different tenses, the participial verbs within them (that is, “ni” and “si”) change and take the form of the verb “kuwa,” as seen in these examples: Musa was a teacher, the town of Msoma was smaller than the town of Mwanza, this young man was not honest, I was not a student. We see here that: (i) -pig- is the root of the word tutampiganisha. (ii) tu-ta-m- are the affixes that come before the root –pig-. (iii) –an-ish-a are the affixes that come after the root –pig-. The prefixes and suffixes of the root -pig- give different meanings, as follows: (i) The prefix tu- indicates first person plural (we). (ii) The prefix -ta- indicates future tense. (iii) The prefix -m- refers to the object, third person singular (him/her). (iv) The affix -an- indicates reciprocity. (v) The affix –ish- is the causative marker. (vi) The affix -a is for finalizing the verb form. (b) Derivational or formative affixes normally occur at the end of the stem of the word. According to these scholars, a verb is a word that describes an action. The verb carries the noun and indicates what it wants to do and at what time. However, derivation is the process of increasing a word’s ability to be used in various contexts and generating new vocabulary different from the original, even though its root remains unchanged. Also, derivation refers to words that share the same root but can distinguish themselves through different forms and generate new vocabulary. These affixes serve three functions: (i) to expand the meaning of a word, (ii) to construct the root or stem for derivation, and (iii) to change a word from one class to another. Vitenzi, Kiafrika, Kimasaba. Katika makala hii, mtafiti anaeleza jinsi vitenzi katika lugha za Kiafrika vinavyoundwa ili kuwasilisha maana tofauti. Hili linafanyika kwa kurejelea Kimasaba, lugha inayozungumzwa na watu wa Masaba nchini Uganda. Uundaji wa vitenzi ni jambo la kawaida na hufanyika katika lugha mbalimbali. Mbinu ya utafiti ilikuwa ya msingi wa uwanjani. Kwa kutumia mbinu hii, mtafiti alitembelea uwanjani ambapo alihoji wahojiwa wake. Majibu ya wahojiwa ndiyo yalikuwa data iliyohitajika na mtafiti. Kwa kumalizia, matokeo ya utafiti huu yanaonyesha kwamba Kimasaba, kama ilivyo kwa lugha nyingine za Kiafrika, ina idadi kubwa ya vitenzi vilivyoundwa ambavyo hurahisisha mazungumzo ya wasemaji wake. Kwa sababu ya pengo hili, mtafiti aliamua kuendeleza utafiti huu kwa lengo la kufafanua hali ilivyo katika Kimasaba. Hii ni kwa sababu lugha nyingi za wachache zimepotea kutokana na kutofanyiwa utafiti, na nyingine zinaendelea kutoweka. MBINU ZA UTAFITI  
Kitenzi ni neno linaloelezea hali ya tendo. Kitenzi kimoja kinaweza kutokana na kuelezea hali tofauti za matendo. Kwa kawaida, kuna aina kama vile mnyambuliko wa mtendaji, mwangamano, mwendeshajiwa, usimaji, na mnyambuliko wa kusababisha katika lugha nyingi za Kibantu. Hivyo basi, katika kazi hii, mtafiti anataja vitenzi mbalimbali vya Kimasaba, ambayo ni lugha ya Bamasaaba, na kuvijumuisha kwa Kiswahili. Inapaswa kuelezwa mapema kuwa kuna lahaja tofauti za Kimasaba. Kwa hivyo, katika utafiti huu, mtafiti alilenga lahaja maalum ijulikanayo kama ‘Lubuuya.’ Baada ya kutafsiri vitenzi hivi, mtafiti anaeleza mchakato wa uundaji wa vitenzi. Baada ya kuelezea jinsi vitenzi hivi vinavyoundwa, mtafiti anafafanua jinsi vinavyotumika katika sentensi. Mtafiti anafanya hivyo kwa kuzingatia maelezo ya waandishi mbalimbali kuhusu uundaji wa vitenzi. Hatimaye, mtafiti anahitimisha kazi hii kwa kutoa mtazamo wake kuhusu mambo muhimu yanayohusiana na utafiti huu. SWALI LA UTAFITI  
Katika utafiti huu, mtafiti alitumia mbinu ya mahojiano. Kwa kutumia mbinu hii, mtafiti alikwenda uwanjani kukutana na wahojiwa. Kabla ya kufanya mahojiano hayo, mtafiti aliwaeleza wahojiwa lengo la utafiti. Baada ya kufanya hivyo, mtafiti aliendelea kufanya mahojiano nao. Wahojiwa walikuwa na wanawake 50 na wanaume 50. Mtafiti alihakikisha kuwa idadi ya wanawake na wanaume ilikuwa sawa kutokana na suala la usawa wa kijinsia. Wahojiwa hawa walichaguliwa kwa kutumia mbinu ya kuchagua makusudi. Kwa kutumia mbinu hii, mtafiti aliendelea na mazungumzo na wahojiwa kila alipokutana nao. Hakutumia utaratibu maalum katika kuchagua wahojiwa. Mtafiti alikuwa na seti ya maswali aliyotumia wakati wa mahojiano. Mtafiti alitumia mwongozo huu ili kuhakikisha kwamba hakusahau mambo muhimu yoyote. Majadiliano yaliyofanyika yalijikita zaidi kwenye uundaji wa vitenzi. Baada ya kutaja kitenzi, mtafiti aliuliza jinsi ya kukitengeneza katika muktadha mbalimbali. Kulingana na mtafiti, kuna makundi mengi ya kikabila barani Afrika. Kila kundi la kikabila lina lugha yake ya asili. Kwa hiyo, kuna lugha nyingi zinazozungumzwa kote barani humo. Hata hivyo, lugha hizi nyingi bado hazijafanyiwa utafiti, na kuna mambo mengi yanayobebwa na lugha hizi ambayo bado hayajulikani duniani. Kuna lugha chache sana za Kiafrika ambazo zimefanyiwa utafiti wa kina.

Kwa mfano, kutoka kwenye mzizi pig-, tunapata neno ‘piga’ ambalo ni kitenzi. Na tukitengeneza neno hili, tunapata maneno kama pigana, piganisha, pigika, ambapo kila moja lina maana tofauti. Kutoka kwenye mzizi wa kitenzi pend-, tunaweza kupata maneno kama yale yaliyoorodheshwa hapo juu, ambapo viambishi –e, -an, -ele, -esh ni vya uambatisho, kwa kuwa vinatengeneza vitenzi vyenye maana tofauti. Kiswahili kina viambishi vinane vya uundaji wa vitenzi ambavyo huambatanishwa na mizizi ya vitenzi kama ilivyoonyeshwa hapo juu. Viambishi vya uambatisho ni kama ifuatavyo: (a). –w (b) –ik / -ek (c) –ish-/-iz-/-esh-/-ez- (d) –il- (e) –o-/-u (f) –am- (g) –an- (h) –at Wahiga (1999) anaeleza kwamba neno ‘uambatisho’ limetokana na vitenzi viwili. TUKI (2004) inaeleza kwamba uambatisho ni mchakato wa kuongeza viambishi kwenye vitenzi ili kutoa maana tofauti. Mchakato huu ndio unaoitwa uundaji wa vitenzi. Kwa mujibu wa wasomi hawa, kitenzi kina sehemu kuu, ambayo ni mzizi, na kinaruhusu uongezaji wa viambishi mwanzoni au mwishoni mwa neno. Matei (2008) anasema kwamba kati ya aina zote za maneno, kitenzi ndicho kinachoashiria tendo ambalo limefanywa au linafanywa. Anaendelea kueleza kwamba kitenzi kinaweza kuonyesha hali mbalimbali kutokana na uambatisho. Ameweza kugawa vitenzi katika makundi mawili: vitenzi vya matendo na vitenzi vinavyoonyesha umiliki. Kihore na wenzake (2003) wanagawanya vitenzi katika aina kuu tatu: kitenzi kikuu (T), kitenzi msaidizi (Ts), na kitenzi cha kishirikishi (t). Wanaeleza kwamba kitenzi kikuu ni kitenzi kinachoweza kujitokeza pekee katika sentensi na kukamilisha maana yake yenyewe. Kwa mfano: yeye amelala, tutampiga Juma, Khamis atamwona Musa kesho. Kitenzi msaidizi ni kitenzi kinachojitokeza pamoja na kitenzi kuu katika sentensi, kama katika mifano ifuatayo: alikuwa analala, tunapenda kula, Juma alitaka kutudhulumu mali yetu. Mifano hii inaonyesha kwamba vitenzi wasaidizi kwa kawaida hutangulia, kisha kufuatiwa na vitenzi kuu. Mwaka 2008, uambatisho ni neno ambalo maana yake imetokana na maana za maneno mawili: (i) "Kunyambua," ambalo lina maana ya kukata vipandevipande; (ii) "Kunyumbua," likimaanisha kunyoosha na kuvuta kitu chenye kubebeka kwa urahisi, kama vile kamba ya mpira. Katika sarufi, uambatisho ni uwezo wa mzizi au shina kuongezewa kiambishi mwanzoni au mwishoni. Matokeo yake ni kupanua maana ya neno husika. Hii ndiyo kazi ya kila kiambishi—kujenga mizizi na mishina mipya ya maneno, ambayo huitwa mishina au mizizi ya uambatisho. Tunaweza pia kusema kuwa hii ndiyo kazi ya viambishi vya uambatisho au viambishi vya uundaji. Mara nyingi, viambishi vya uundaji huonekana mwishoni mwa shina au mzizi. Kwa hiyo, vimeendelea kuitwa viambishi vya uundaji vinavyoongezwa mwishoni. Katika muktadha huu, uambatisho unahusisha aina mbili za viambishi: (a) Viambishi vya Kisemantiki, ambavyo hujitokeza mwanzoni mwa mzizi wa neno. Viambishi hivi vinaweza kupanua maana ya neno bila kubadilisha mzizi wake. Kwa mfano: tu-ta-m-pig-an-ish-a. Kitenzi cha kishirikishi, ambacho huchukua umbo sawa na “ni” au “si”, huchukuliwa kama kinalinganisha vipengele vingine katika sentensi. Mfano: Musa ni mwalimu, mji wa Msoma ni mdogo kuliko mji wa Mwanza, kijana huyu si mkweli, mimi si mwanafunzi. Kulingana na muktadha wa sentensi hizi, inaonekana kwamba vipengele hivi huchukuliwa kama vinavyolinganisha vipashio vya upande wa kushoto na wa kulia wa kitenzi chenyewe. Sentensi hizi ziko katika wakati uliopo. Iwapo sentensi hizi zitabadilishwa na kuwekwa katika nyakati tofauti, vitenzi vya kishirikishi vilivyomo ndani yake (yaani, “ni” na “si”) hubadilika na kuchukua umbo la kitenzi “kuwa,” kama inavyoonekana kwenye mifano hii: Musa alikuwa mwalimu, mji wa Msoma ulikuwa mdogo kuliko mji wa Mwanza, kijana huyu hakuwa mkweli, sikuwa mwanafunzi. Tunaona hapa kwamba: (i) -pig- ni mzizi wa neno tutampiganisha. (ii) tu-ta-m- ni viambishi vinavyokuja kabla ya mzizi –pig-. (iii) –an-ish-a ni viambishi vinavyokuja baada ya mzizi –pig-. Viambishi vya awali na vya mwishoni vya mzizi -pig- vinatoa maana tofauti, kama ifuatavyo: (i) Kiambishi awali tu- kinaonesha nafsi ya kwanza wingi (sisi). (ii) Kiambishi awali -ta- kinaonesha wakati ujao. (iii) Kiambishi awali -m- kinamhusu kiwakilishi, nafsi ya tatu umoja (yeye). (iv) Kiambishi -an- kinaonesha hali ya kufanyiana (rekipro). (v) Kiambishi –ish- ni kiashiria cha sababishaji. (vi) Kiambishi -a ni cha kukamilisha umbo la kitenzi. (b) Viambishi vya uundaji au vya uambatisho kwa kawaida vinawekwa mwishoni mwa shina la neno. Kwa mujibu wa wataalamu hawa, kitenzi ni neno linaloeleza tendo. Kitenzi hubeba nomino na kuonyesha inachotaka kufanya na wakati gani. Hata hivyo, uambatisho ni mchakato wa kuongeza uwezo wa neno kutumika katika muktadha mbalimbali na kuzalisha msamiati mpya tofauti na ule wa awali, ingawa mzizi wake unabaki vilevile. Vilevile, uambatisho unarejelea maneno yanayoshirikiana mzizi mmoja lakini yanaweza kujitofautisha kupitia maumbo tofauti na kutoa msamiati mpya. Viambishi hivi vinafanya kazi tatu: (i) kupanua maana ya neno, (ii) kujenga mzizi au shina kwa uundaji wa neno, na (iii) kubadilisha neno kutoka daraja moja hadi jingine. This is done by referring to Masaaba, a language spoken by the Masaaba people in Uganda. Verb derivation is a common phenomenon and is practiced in various languages. Therefore, in this article, the researcher describes the verb derivation process in the Masaaba language. He presents a collection of verbs and explains how speakers derive them. In addition, the researcher discusses how these verbs are used in sentences. The researcher does this because many African languages have not been studied, and there are many fascinating aspects that are unknown to the world. In this work, the researcher writes various verbs in the original language and then translates them into Swahili. The aim of this study is, firstly, to demonstrate the process of verb derivation in Masaaba; secondly, to explain the different meanings that result from verb derivation; and thirdly, to show that Masaaba is a language that continues to grow like other African languages.

discourses.source_txt: For example, from the root pig-, we get the word ‘piga’ which is a verb. From the verb root pend-, we can obtain words like those listed above, where the suffixes –e, -an, -ele, -esh are derivational, as they make the forms in question into verbs with different meanings. discourses.source_txt: Matei (2008) states that among all types of words, the verb is the one that indicates the action that has been done or is being done. discourses.source_txt: Kihore and colleagues (2003) divide verbs into three main types: the main verb (T), the auxiliary verb (Ts), and the participial verb (t). They explain that a main verb is a verb that can appear independently in a sentence and complete the meaning on its own.
discourses.translated_txt: Kihore na wenzake (2003) wanagawanya vitenzi katika aina kuu tatu: kitenzi kikuu (T), kitenzi msaidizi (Ts), na kitenzi cha kishirikishi (t). Wanaeleza kwamba kitenzi kikuu ni kitenzi kinachoweza kujitokeza pekee katika sentensi na kukamilisha maana yake yenyewe.

discourses.source_txt: For example: he is sleeping, we will beat Juma, Khamis will see Musa tomorrow.

discourses.source_txt: An auxiliary verb is a verb that appears alongside the main verb in a sentence, as in the following examples: alikuwa analala (he was sleeping), tunapenda kula (we like to eat), Juma alitaka kutudhulumu mali yetu (Juma wanted to defraud us of our property). These examples show that auxiliary verbs usually come first, followed by the main verbs.
discourses.translated_txt: Kitenzi msaidizi ni kitenzi kinachojitokeza pamoja na kitenzi kuu katika sentensi, kama katika mifano ifuatayo: alikuwa analala, tunapenda kula, Juma alitaka kutudhulumu mali yetu. Mifano hii inaonyesha kwamba vitenzi wasaidizi kwa kawaida hutangulia, kisha kufuatiwa na vitenzi kuu.

discourses.source_txt: In grammar, derivation is the ability of a root or stem to be affixed with a morpheme at its beginning or end.

discourses.source_txt: The result is to expand the meaning of the given word. This is the function of every affix—to build new roots and stems of words, which are called derivational stems or roots. We can also say that this is the function of derivational affixes or formative affixes.

discourses.source_txt: A participial verb, which takes the same form as “ni” or “si”, is considered to link other elements in a sentence.
discourses.translated_txt: Kitenzi cha kishirikishi, ambacho huchukua umbo sawa na “ni” au “si”, huchukuliwa kama kinalinganisha vipengele vingine katika sentensi.

discourses.source_txt: If these sentences are changed to different tenses, the participial verbs within them (that is, “ni” and “si”) change and take the form of the verb “kuwa,” as seen in these examples: Musa was a teacher, the town of Msoma was smaller than the town of Mwanza, this young man was not honest, I was not a student.

discourses.source_txt: We see here that: (i) -pig- is the root of the word tutampiganisha. (ii) tu-ta-m- are the affixes that come before the root –pig-. (ii) The prefix -ta- indicates future tense. (iii) The prefix -m- refers to the object, third person singular (him/her). (iv) The affix -an- indicates reciprocity. (v) The affix –ish- is the causative marker. (vi) The affix -a is for finalizing the verb form. (b) Derivational or formative affixes normally occur at the end of the stem of the word.

Mbwillow (2017) explains that words in human languages are formed in various ways. He mentions methods such as reduplication, coining, compounding, and affixation, referring specifically to inflection and derivation. He explains that affixation is the process of attaching or adding morphemes or affixes before or after the root, core, or stem of a word. He emphasizes that the main methods of word formation are inflection and derivation. He defines derivation as the process of attaching morphemes/affixes after the root and stem of a word. In his work, he states that inflection and derivation form new words. He clarifies that inflection and derivation may not necessarily change the word class but rather expand the meaning of the word in question. This includes the possibility for the action of a verb to be possible, for example: someka, imbika, ombeka, fungika.

discourses.source_txt: The literature also shows that there are many scholars who have written about verb derivation in languages. Some scholars have written about verb derivation in the Swahili language, while others have written about verb derivation in other African languages such as Kinyakyusa, Kigiryama, Kigichugu, and so on.
discourses.translated_txt: Fasihi pia inaonesha kwamba kuna wataalamu wengi ambao wameandika kuhusu uundaji wa vitenzi katika lugha mbalimbali. discourses.source_txt: However, there is no evidence that any scholar has written about verb derivation in Kimasaaba.
discourses.translated_txt: Hata hivyo, hakuna ushahidi kwamba mtaalamu yeyote ameandika kuhusu uundaji wa vitenzi katika Kimasaba.

discourses.source_txt: The writings of various scholars demonstrate that a verb is a word that expresses an action, whereas derivation is the process of adding affixes to a verb to generate new words with different meanings. Various texts also indicate that there are different types of verb derivation. These types include the active voice, the applicative, the reciprocal, the stative, the causative, and the mutual applicative forms.
discourses.translated_txt: Maandishi ya wataalamu mbalimbali yanaonesha kwamba kitenzi ni neno linaloonyesha tendo, ilhali uundaji ni mchakato wa kuongeza viambishi kwenye kitenzi ili kutoa maneno mapya yenye maana tofauti. Matini mbalimbali pia zinaonesha kuwa kuna aina tofauti za uundaji wa vitenzi. Aina hizi ni pamoja na hali ya tambuzi, umbo la applicative, umbo la rekhiprochai, umbo la statici, umbo la sababishaji, na umbo la mutual applicable.

Based on the findings of this study, it is clear that African languages, especially Bantu languages, allow for the application of verb inflection.

discourses.source_txt: Kimasaaba, as one of the African languages, does allow for verb inflection. This verb inflection facilitates communication with ease. This is because speakers of the language can use a single word to convey different meanings. If speakers of the language do not have the ability to inflect verbs, they will not be fully proficient in the grammar of Kiswahili: questions and exercises.
discourses.translated_txt: Kimasaaba, kama mojawapo ya lugha za Kiafrika, huruhusu viambishi vya vitenzi. Viambishi hivi vya vitenzi hufanya mawasiliano kuwa rahisi. Ikiwa wazungumzaji wa lugha hiyo hawana uwezo wa kuweka viambishi katika vitenzi, hawatakuwa na ujuzi kamili wa sarufi ya Kiswahili: maswali na mazoezi.
